Each of the six portfolio companies gets a named operating system built from proven vendors plus a thin BSP data layer, not custom software. The goal is to make earnings look more recurring, predictable and scalable to the next buyer. The evidence supports up to ~3 turns of quality premium, of which tech can claim about 0.5-2.5 turns depending on the company (ServiceOS evidence, Oct 6, 2026).

# Tech-enablement theses by portfolio company

Each of the six portfolio companies gets a named operating system built from proven vendors plus a thin BSP data layer, not custom software. The goal is to make earnings look more recurring, predictable and scalable to the next buyer. The evidence supports up to ~3 turns of quality premium, of which tech can claim about 0.5-2.5 turns depending on the company (ServiceOS evidence, Oct 6, 2026).

## Theses at a glance

| Company | OS and core stack | Thesis | Premium (est., turns) | Agent value (est., $M/yr) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Punctual Pros | ServiceOS (ServiceTitan) | Lift booking rates, ticket size and membership density | 1.0-2.5 | 0.88 |
| CET | GridOS (Procore) | Turn project work into recurring solar/SCADA and EV O&M | 0.5-1.5 | 1.32 |
| Frontline | FirmOS (ConnectWise/Kaseya) | Grow security and e-billing revenue-cycle lines | 0.5-1.5 | 3.59 |
| Thomas Scientific | LabOS (Shopify Plus/Coupa) | Raise EBITDA via digital share and lower cost-to-serve | 0.5-1.0 | 3.84 |
| BPI | SignalOS (Brandwatch/Zignal) | Productize monitoring; draft faster under confidentiality | 0.5-2.0 | 2.27 |
| Fair Harbor | HarborOS (Shopify/Klaviyo) | Cut returns and excess inventory | not shown in extract | 0.77 |

Sources: ServiceOS evidence; Portfolio AI-agent plan.

## Where evidence is strongest

- **Punctual Pros is the lead case.** HVAC booking rates average 38% versus 59% at 25+ technician shops. Pricebook adopters grew tickets 14% vs 8%. Evidence is strong on direction and medium on size (ServiceOS evidence).
- **Scale drives most of the big multiples.** Champions (~18.5x) and Sila (~17x) are press estimates and mostly reflect density and M&A runway (ServiceOS evidence).
- **Mature margin target.** A mid-teens EBITDA margin is realistic. Installers grow only ~2-4%, so recurring service agreements matter (Public comparables).

## Where evidence is weaker

- **Thomas Scientific.** The case is EBITDA, not multiple. It is benchmarked to Avantor's ~80% digital transactions and Grainger's ~15.6% digital growth vs ~2% rep-led growth. Leverage drives that exit (ServiceOS evidence).
- **Frontline.** Entry was already ~12-15x (est.), which limits re-rating headroom (ServiceOS evidence).
- **CET.** Electrical M&A slowed to 99 deals in 2025, so buyers are more selective (ServiceOS evidence).
- **Fair Harbor.** The premium range is truncated in the extract. The full ServiceOS evidence file would answer it.

## Caveats

- Agent values total ~$12.7M (est.). They are not de-duplicated. Volumes are analyst assumptions (Portfolio AI-agent plan).
- Many metric claims come from vendor case studies.

## Next actions

- Replace the assumed call, ticket, invoice and member volumes with system-of-record counts at each portfolio company before wave 1.
- Pull the full HarborOS and SignalOS sections to fill the Fair Harbor premium range and BPI detail.
- Baseline booking rate, average ticket and membership count at Punctual Pros now, so ServiceOS gains are measurable at exit.
- Build the Thomas Scientific case on EBITDA and cost-to-serve, not multiple expansion.
